316	  /// A split group title bar addressed by its member's name (labels are `"<project>, workroom <name>"`).
317	  private func memberTitleBar(_ app: XCUIApplication, labelled name: String) -> XCUIElement {

329	  /// trailing edge. The tolerance is a couple of points (stroke width + rounding); the fault it catches
330	  /// was ~48pt.
331	  func testEachSplitGroupBracketFramesItsOwnChips() throws {

333	    app.launchArguments += [
334	      "-WorkroomUITestFixture", "1",
335	      "-WorkroomUITestWorkroomSplit", "1",
336	      "-WorkroomUITestSecondWorkroomSplit", "1",

338	      "-ApplePersistenceIgnoreState", "YES",

353	    let roomTwo = workroomChip(app, named: "uitest-room-2")
354	    let roomThree = workroomChip(app, named: "uitest-room-3")

356	      XCTAssertTrue(chip.exists, "every member chip is in the bar")

362	      "group A's bracket starts at its first member's chip, not inside a neighbour")
363	    XCTAssertEqual(
364	      bracketA.frame.maxX, roomOne.frame.maxX, accuracy: tolerance,
365	      "…and ends at its last member's chip")
366	    XCTAssertEqual(

1	import SwiftUI
2	
3	/// The detail pane's terminals for one target (a workroom or a project root): a horizontal
4	/// tab strip below the title bar plus the active terminal. Observes `TerminalSessions` so
5	/// adding, closing, and switching tabs all update live.
6	///
7	/// This view coordinates the tab strip (`TerminalTabStrip`) and the pane content
8	/// (`PaneTreeView`), owning the cross-component drag-into-pane wiring: `chipPaneDrag` (the live
9	/// drop preview the pane tree renders) and `contentFrame` (the pane area's global rect, used to
10	/// tell "over the strip" reorder from "over a pane" drop-to-split and to localise the cursor).
11	/// The strip is handed those via a binding plus the `chipLocal`/`chipDropTarget` closures.
12	struct WorkroomTerminalsView: View {
13	  let target: TerminalTarget
14	  @ObservedObject var sessions: TerminalSessions
15	  /// Whether this workroom's terminal may hold keyboard focus — `false` for a co-displayed but
16	  /// non-focused split member, so it doesn't steal first responder (and the workroom selection) on mount.
17	  var surfaceActive: Bool = true
18	  @EnvironmentObject var notifications: NotificationCenterStore
19	  @EnvironmentObject var store: AppStore
20	  @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
21	
22	  // Drag a tab chip down into a pane to split (issue #3). `chipPaneDrag` is the live drop preview
23	  // (content-local), shown by `PaneTreeView`; `contentFrame` is the pane area's global rect, used to
24	  // tell "over the strip" (reorder) from "over a pane" (drop-to-split) and to localise the cursor.
25	  @State private var chipPaneDrag: PaneDragState?
26	  @State private var contentFrame: CGRect = .zero
27	
28	  var body: some View {
29	    let tabs = sessions.tabs(for: target)
30	    let active = sessions.activeTab(for: target)
31	    // The terminal (or empty state) fills the pane; the tab bar rides on safeAreaInset so it only
32	    // ever takes its natural height — otherwise the tab bar's horizontal ScrollView grabs the
33	    // vertical slack when there's no terminal below it and balloons.
34	    Group {
35	      if let active {
36	        // Always render through the one pane tree — a solo terminal is just a single-leaf layout.
37	        // Routing solo and split through the SAME host means a surface has exactly one owner; an
38	        // earlier split→solo bug came from two `TerminalContainerView`s (the solo branch and the dying
39	        // split leaf) fighting over the same surface and stranding it in a detached container (#3).
40	        PaneTreeView(
41	          layout: contentLayout(active: active), target: target, sessions: sessions,
42	          externalDrag: chipPaneDrag, surfaceActive: surfaceActive
43	        )
44	        .background(
45	          GeometryReader { geo in
46	            Color.clear.preference(key: ContentFrameKey.self, value: geo.frame(in: .global))
47	          }
48	        )
49	      } else {
50	        ContentUnavailableView {
51	          Label("No terminal", systemImage: "terminal")
52	        } description: {
53	          Text("Open one with ⌘T.")
54	        } actions: {
55	          Button("New Terminal") { sessions.addTab(for: target) }
56	            .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
57	            // Use the active theme accent rather than the system blue (issue #36).
58	            .tint(ThemeService.shared.tokens.accent)
59	            .accessibilityIdentifier("NewTerminal")
60	        }
61	      }
62	    }
63	    // A thin 2pt frame inside the workroom's card, so the card's lighter fill reads as a border rather
64	    // than a margin. Top is 0 so the tab strip sits flush on the content (the active tab bridges the
65	    // panel→bg colour step) — the Chrome-style merge with the strip above. Applied to the whole Group,
66	    // not just the pane tree, so the "No terminal" empty state is inset by the same gutter.
67	    .padding(.horizontal, 2)
68	    .padding(.bottom, 2)
69	    .padding(.top, 0)
70	    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
71	    .onPreferenceChange(ContentFrameKey.self) { contentFrame = $0 }
72	    .safeAreaInset(edge: .top, spacing: 0) {
73	      // No tab bar when there are no terminals: the empty state's "New Terminal" button (and ⌘T) cover
74	      // adding one, so the strip and its "+" would be redundant. A split member's remove-from-split ✕
75	      // now lives in its pane title bar (issue #110), drawn by the leaf above this view and present
76	      // even with zero tabs — so the strip no longer needs to stay alive just to host the ✕.
77	      if !tabs.isEmpty {
78	        TerminalTabStrip(
79	          tabs: tabs, activeID: active?.id, target: target, sessions: sessions,
80	          chipPaneDrag: $chipPaneDrag,
81	          localize: { chipLocal($0) },
82	          dropTarget: { chipDropTarget(at: $0) }
83	        )
84	        // A backgrounded workroom (`!surfaceActive` — a non-focused workroom *split* member, or a
85	        // backgrounded solo workroom, issue #82) dims its terminals via the per-pane scrim in
86	        // `PaneTreeView`. That scrim covers only the Metal surfaces, not this tab strip — it rides on
87	        // the safe-area inset, outside the pane tree — so without this the strip stayed bright while
88	        // its panes faded. The strip is plain SwiftUI (no Metal layer), so a plain `.opacity` fade is
89	        // enough; match the scrim's `surfaceActive` animation so the strip and panes fade together.
90	        .opacity(surfaceActive ? 1 : 0.45)
91	        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .easeInOut(duration: 0.07), value: surfaceActive)
92	      }
93	    }
94	    // Create the first terminal once the pane appears (and for each new target), then reconcile
95	    // occlusion so the right surfaces render after a target switch (issue #3).
96	    .task(id: target.id) {
97	      // Through the store so a pending auto-run (issue #7) suppresses the default first tab and the
98	      // run command becomes tab #1 instead of being orphaned beside a stray "Terminal 1".
99	      store.ensureInitialTerminal(for: target)
100	      sessions.reconcileOcclusion(for: target)
101	    }
102	    // Focusing a terminal dismisses its notifications — but ONLY while this view is the focused one
103	    // (`surfaceActive`). In a workroom split EVERY member renders through this view, including
104	    // co-displayed NON-focused members (`surfaceActive: false`, issue #23); without the gate, such a
105	    // member would wipe its OWN notifications on mount/remount via the `initial: true` fire — a pane
106	    // you're explicitly not looking at (issue #89). With the gate: for the focused member, `active.id`
107	    // changing *is* a focus change (chip tap, ⌘1–9, sidebar switch, close revealing a neighbour) and
108	    // `initial` handles its first appearance. The sibling `surfaceActive` hook covers selection
109	    // MOVING to a member — `selectedTargetID` changes but the member's `active.id` does not, so the
110	    // hook above wouldn't fire. In the single-workroom path `surfaceActive` is always true, so this
111	    // behaves exactly as before. Returning to the app with the same tab focused is handled separately
112	    // by RootView's didBecomeActive → dismissFocusedTerminalNotifications.
113	    .onChange(of: active?.id, initial: true) { _, id in
114	      if surfaceActive, let id { notifications.dismiss(tab: id) }
115	    }
116	    .onChange(of: surfaceActive) { _, nowFocused in
117	      if nowFocused, let id = active?.id { notifications.dismiss(tab: id) }
118	    }
119	    // All three AND in `!store.hasModalPresentation` for the same reason RootView's booleans do: a
120	    // menu key equivalent still fires while a dialog or sheet is up, so ⌘W / ⌘F / ⌘↑ / ⌘↓ / ⌘D would
121	    // otherwise act on the terminal behind it. Disabling the item drops the key equivalent.
122	    //
123	    // Drive the "Close Terminal" menu command's enabled state.
124	    .focusedSceneValue(\.hasTerminal, !tabs.isEmpty && !store.hasModalPresentation)
125	    // Drive the Go-menu Previous/Next Terminal Tab items (issue #29) — only meaningful with ≥2 tabs.
126	    .focusedSceneValue(\.multipleTerminalTabs, tabs.count > 1 && !store.hasModalPresentation)
127	    // Drive View ▸ "Resize Splits Evenly" (issue #83) — only when a terminal split is on screen. Note
128	    // that in a workroom split EVERY member mounts this view, so all three of these are written by
129	    // several instances at once and the last writer wins; the menu items they drive are all
130	    // "is such a thing on screen at all", for which any visible member is an acceptable answer. A
131	    // blocking setup script withholds this view, so no item can act on a hidden split.
132	    .focusedSceneValue(
133	      \.terminalSplitVisible,
134	      sessions.isSplitVisible(for: target) && !store.hasModalPresentation)
135	  }
136	
137	  /// The layout the content area renders: the split when it's visible, else the focused solo tab.
138	  private func contentLayout(active: TerminalTab) -> TerminalPaneLayout {
139	    sessions.isSplitVisible(for: target)
140	      ? (sessions.split(for: target) ?? .leaf(active.id)) : .leaf(active.id)
141	  }
142	
143	  /// The content-local point for a chip drag at `global`, or nil when the cursor is outside the pane
144	  /// area (i.e. still over the strip → a reorder, not a drop-into-pane).
145	  private func chipLocal(_ global: CGPoint) -> CGPoint? {
146	    guard contentFrame.contains(global) else { return nil }
147	    return CGPoint(x: global.x - contentFrame.minX, y: global.y - contentFrame.minY)
148	  }
149	
150	  /// Where a chip dropped at `global` lands (pane + edge), using the same pane plan the renderer uses,
151	  /// or nil if it isn't over a pane.
152	  private func chipDropTarget(at global: CGPoint) -> (tab: TerminalTab.ID, edge: PaneEdge)? {
153	    guard let local = chipLocal(global), let active = sessions.activeTab(for: target) else {
154	      return nil
155	    }
156	    let plan = PaneTreeLayout.plan(
157	      contentLayout(active: active), in: CGRect(origin: .zero, size: contentFrame.size))
158	    return PaneTreeLayout.dropTarget(at: local, panes: plan.panes)
159	  }
160	}
161	
162	/// The pane area's global frame — lets the strip localise a chip drag and tell "over the strip"
163	/// (reorder) from "over a pane" (drop-to-split).
164	private struct ContentFrameKey: PreferenceKey {
165	  static var defaultValue: CGRect = .zero
166	  static func reduce(value: inout CGRect, nextValue: () -> CGRect) {
167	    let next = nextValue()
168	    if next != .zero { value = next }
169	  }
170	}

input.description: "Split Right" menu item confirmed enabled=true via diagnostic assertion — hasTerminal FocusedValue theory was wrong. Real cause: TerminalSessions.fits() refuses a split when the halved pane would drop below minPaneWidth(300)*2+dividerThickness(4)=604pt. UITestFixture.applyFixtureDefaults has always forced the right inspector open (300pt); the new sidebarVisible fixture force adds the sidebar (270pt) on top. At the 1200pt fixture window width, detail column shrank to ~630pt — right on the fits() floor with no real-world margin. Fixed by widening the fixture window to 1450pt (AppStore.swift ~line 1110), leaving ~880pt for the detail column: clears the 604pt split floor with room, and stays under the ~1000pt tab-strip overflow tests need to still overflow. Diagnostic print removed from SplitPaneUITests.swift.

Fixed by widening the fixture window to 1450pt (AppStore.swift ~line 1110), leaving ~880pt for the detail column: clears the 604pt split floor with room, and stays under the ~1000pt tab-strip overflow tests need to still overflow. content.description: "Split Right" menu item confirmed enabled=true via diagnostic assertion — hasTerminal FocusedValue theory was wrong. Real cause: TerminalSessions.fits() refuses a split when the halved pane would drop below minPaneWidth(300)*2+dividerThickness(4)=604pt. UITestFixture.applyFixtureDefaults has always forced the right inspector open (300pt); the new sidebarVisible fixture force adds the sidebar (270pt) on top. At the 1200pt fixture window width, detail column shrank to ~630pt — right on the fits() floor with no real-world margin. Fixed by widening the fixture window to 1450pt (AppStore.swift ~line 1110), leaving ~880pt for the detail column: clears the 604pt split floor with room, and stays under the ~1000pt tab-strip overflow tests need to still overflow. Diagnostic print removed from SplitPaneUITests.swift.

content.subject: Root-caused: not a focus race, a geometry floor
content.description: "Split Right" menu item confirmed enabled=true via diagnostic assertion — hasTerminal FocusedValue theory was wrong. Real cause: TerminalSessions.fits() refuses a split when the halved pane would drop below minPaneWidth(300)*2+dividerThickness(4)=604pt. UITestFixture.applyFixtureDefaults has always forced the right inspector open (300pt); the new sidebarVisible fixture force adds the sidebar (270pt) on top. At the 1200pt fixture window width, detail column shrank to ~630pt — right on the fits() floor with no real-world margin. Fixed by widening the fixture window to 1450pt (AppStore.swift ~line 1110), leaving ~880pt for the detail column: clears the 604pt split floor with room, and stays under the ~1000pt tab-strip overflow tests need to still overflow. Diagnostic print removed from SplitPaneUITests.swift.

content.subject: Verify geometry fix (1450pt window) across all affected classes
content.description: All 13+ discriminating tests now pass. Root causes: (1) fits() geometry floor fixed by widening fixture window 1200→1450pt; (2) DiffViewerUITests.testSideBySideRendersTwoColumns fixed by pinning sidebarWidth/inspectorWidth in UITestFixture.applyFixtureDefaults (real domain had drifted to 406/281 from an old drag-resize test, pushing detail column under DiffViewer.sideBySideMinWidth=700); (3) WorkroomWorkflowUITests.testAppLaunchesWithChrome fixed by (a) gating persistsSidebarPrefs on !UITestFixture.isActive so future fixture toggles stop polluting the real Dev domain, and (b) one-time restore of the currently-stuck real sidebar.visible default back to true. All confirmed via xcresulttool.

The search results show information related to macOS display/screen lock behavior and XCUITest automation issues, though not specifically focused on all aspects of your query. Here's what I found:

**macOS Screen Lock and Display Sleep:**

Control+Command+Q locks the whole session on Mac, and the screen locks instantly and requires your password or Touch ID to return. However, a full session lock gets in the way when workflows need the session to stay live, as GUI-driving agents that click, type, and read the screen can't see or touch a locked interface.

To prevent automatic sleeping, you can configure macOS with "Prevent automatic sleeping on power adapter when the display is off" set to on, and "Require password after screen saver begins or display is turned off" set to never.

**XCUITest Automation Issues:**

The search results also revealed an issue with XCUITest on iOS 18: When XCUITest encounters an "Application has not loaded accessibility" error after a 60 second timeout, it performs an undocumented auto-recovery instead of halting the test as documented, leaving the XCUITest framework in a corrupted state and causing subsequent tests in the same session to fail.

This appears to be related to flakiness in automation sessions when dealing with system-level states like display sleep and screen locks on macOS.

Based on the search results, here are the known limitations of XCUITest in 2026:

## Platform & Language Limitations

XCUITest only works for native iOS, iPadOS, and macOS apps and can't drive React Native, Flutter, or other cross-platform UI frameworks directly. XCUITest only currently supports Objective-C and Swift.

## WebView & System UI Limitations

XCUITest does not handle WebView content well, and anything rendered inside a WKWebView is largely invisible to XCUITest. XCUITest can't interact with system dialogs, as permission prompts and notification authorization dialogs are rendered by iOS, not by your app.

## Visual Testing Limitations

XCUITest can capture screen states, but it does not provide native image comparison or baseline management. Minor differences in iOS versions, fonts, or device resolutions can produce inconsistent visual outputs, and maintaining stable reference environments requires strict control over device configuration.

## Execution & Setup Limitations

XCUITest relies on iOS simulators for testing, which might not accurately replicate real device behavior, and simulators may have performance differences and limitations. To run on a physical device, XCUITest needs to be running Xcode on a Mac, which can be especially difficult if the testing setup is working remotely. XCUITest can be relatively slow when compared to other test automation frameworks, which can be a challenge for large test suites, leading to longer test execution times.

I've performed the web search on SwiftUI XCUITest accessibility limitations and focusedSceneValue testing. Here's what I found:

## Key Findings

**XCUITest and Accessibility Integration:**
XCTest utilizes Accessibility APIs to access controls in your view hierarchy and interact with them. UI testing is based on accessibility, so the more accessibility features you add to your app, the easier will be to write UI tests.

**Best Practices:**
- Always assign .accessibilityIdentifier to SwiftUI views you want to test.
- Be sure to check the element's label, this is the same label that VoiceOver will read and Voice Control users will speak.

**Known Limitations:**
Although it has its limitations, there is scope for creating valid accessibility tests using this framework. One specific issue is that on iOS 26.1, a ToolbarItem placed in .keyboard is no longer exposed to the accessibility hierarchy. As a result, VoiceOver cannot focus or activate the toolbar button and XCUITest cannot discover the element, making the UI impossible to test.

Based on the search results, I found relevant information about XCUITest on macOS and some related concepts, though the results primarily focus on iOS testing. Here are the key findings:

**XCUITest Framework Overview:**
XCUITest empowers developers to script automated UI tests using Swift or Objective-C, catering to native iOS and macOS applications.

**Real Device Testing Complexity:**
Automating a real device with XCUITest is considerably more complicated, due to Apple's restrictions around running apps on real devices.

**Keyboard and Mouse Interaction:**
XCUIElement facilitates testing through keyboard and mouse interactions, offering access to various UI components such as tables, alerts, buttons, text labels, and input fields.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about SwiftUI unit testing limitations and how ViewInspector addresses them:

## The Core Problem

Views in SwiftUI are nested inside one another, forming a statically typed hierarchy of structs without an API to inspect the view's content. Views don't expose their internal structure. We can't reach in to tap a button or read a text label.

## A Key Limitation with View State

One significant limitation is testing views with `@State`. It's actually not possible to test the action of clicking the button on the numClicks. The acceptable workaround is to add a bit of code to the view, transforming it basically in [adding] internal let inspection = Inspection<Self>() to enable testing.

## How ViewInspector Helps

ViewInspector is a library for unit testing SwiftUI views. It allows for traversing a view hierarchy at runtime providing direct access to the underlying View structs. It gives us a way to inspect SwiftUI views from our tests — not just examine state, but also trigger actions.

However, since it requires more work to support reacting to view updates dynamically, at least for now, it is used for static views and UI-tests instead for tests simulating user interaction.

content.text:
## XCUITest / SwiftUI UI-test limitations — research summary

**Platform/execution**
- macOS `-destination 'platform=macOS'` drives the REAL machine — actual mouse/keyboard, not a simulator. No headless mode for macOS XCUITest. Confirmed firsthand this session: background test runs took over your physical Mac.
- iOS XCUITest uses simulators/devices; can't run headless either, though simulators isolate from the physical machine.
- Comparatively slow — full suites scale badly, matches our own 35-40min full-suite runtime.

**Accessibility-tree dependent**
- XCUITest sees only what Accessibility exposes. WKWebView content is largely invisible. System dialogs (permission prompts) aren't interactable as app elements.
- SwiftUI's AX exposure has real gaps/regressions across OS versions — e.g. a documented iOS 26.1 regression where `.toolbar(placement: .keyboard)` items stopped exposing to AX, breaking both VoiceOver and XCUITest for that control. Matches our own "SourceKit noise" and AX-timing gotchas (`macapp-xcuitest-gotchas.md`: `.onHover` undrivable, wrapper views unqueryable).

**State isolation — the big one, hit repeatedly this session**
- No sandboxed UserDefaults/preferences domain between test launches. Each XCUIApplication().launch() is a fresh PROCESS but shares the SAME on-disk prefs domain — one test's persisted write (sidebar width, toggle state) leaks into the next launch, same `xcodebuild test` invocation or not. This is exactly what caused today's `sidebarVisible`/`sidebarWidth`/`inspectorWidth` cross-contamination chain.
- No official "reset defaults between tests" primitive — apps must self-defend (our fix: force values in a fixture-mode init path).

**SwiftUI-specific**
- No public API to inspect view internals/state (`@State` etc.) from outside — third-party `ViewInspector` fills gap for VIEW-level unit tests, but doesn't help XCUITest (that's black-box, AX-only anyway).
- `focusedSceneValue`/`@FocusedValue` timing vs literal AppKit first-responder is subtle and under-documented — cost us a wrong hypothesis today before finding the real cause (a geometry floor, not a focus race).
- Layout is genuinely non-deterministic across machines/window sizes unless the app explicitly pins geometry for tests — width-dependent behavior (splits, side-by-side collapse thresholds) breaks silently if window size drifts, which is exactly today's bug.

**Flakiness sources**
- Display sleep / screen lock kills a running automation session outright (locked screen = no synthetic input reaches it). `caffeinate -dis` mitigates but isn't bulletproof.
- Xcode 26 has a documented "Application has not loaded accessibility" 60s-timeout auto-recovery bug that leaves XCUITest in a corrupted state for the REST of the session instead of failing cleanly — could explain some of today's unexplained "killed" runs on long invocations.

Sources:
- [What is XCUITest and why it matters](https://bitrise.io/guides/xcuitest)
- [iOS Automation Testing Tools (2026)](https://www.drizz.dev/post/ios-automation-testing-tools-in-2026)
- [SwiftUI .toolbar(placement: .keyboard) item not exposed to accessibility on iOS 26.1](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/807529)
- [XCUITests for Accessibility](https://medium.com/@r.whitaker/xcuitests-for-accessibility-43c2bde551a5)
- ["Application has not loaded accessibility" timeout auto-recovery corrupts framework state](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/813260)
- [Computer Use locks an unlocked Mac after waking a sleeping display](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/36776)
- [Who said we cannot unit test SwiftUI views?](https://nalexn.github.io/swiftui-unit-testing/)
- [ViewInspector for SwiftUI](https://github.com/nalexn/ViewInspector)

Real cause: TerminalSessions.fits() refuses a split when the halved pane would drop below minPaneWidth(300)*2+dividerThickness(4)=604pt. Fixed by widening the fixture window to 1450pt (AppStore.swift ~line 1110), leaving ~880pt for the detail column: clears the 604pt split floor with room, and stays under the ~1000pt tab-strip overflow tests need to still overflow. Diagnostic print removed from SplitPaneUITests.swift.

## P3 — Tests and tooling

### Deferred UI workflow tests (macapp)

**What:** The two workflow UI tests left to write on top of the now-landed fixture seam:
1. **Notification badge + click-to-navigate** — drive a terminal to `printf '\e]9;…\a'`, assert the
   sidebar/tab badge appears, click it, assert it navigates to (and clears on) the right terminal.
2. **Delete-workroom-clears-badges** — assert deleting a workroom withdraws its notifications/badges.

**Why:** The fixture seam itself is done (`Core/UITestFixture.swift` + `-WorkroomUITestFixture 1`
gives deterministic, CI-able state — see `AppStore.loadFixture()`), and the split-pane + basic
workflow suites pass deterministically (no `XCTSkip`). These two notification/delete flows are the
remaining gap, called out explicitly in `WorkroomWorkflowUITests.swift` ("Still to add: …").

**How to start:** Add the tests to `macapp/WorkroomAppUITests/WorkroomWorkflowUITests.swift` using
the existing fixture launch arg and the `sidebar.*` / `terminal.tab.*` accessibility identifiers. The
badge assertions need the notification a11y identifiers to be queryable — add them if missing.

**Depends on:** the fixture seam + accessibility identifiers already in place
(`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/UITestFixture.swift`, `Views/ProjectSidebar.swift`,
`Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift`).

**Priority:** P3 (the smoke + opportunistic suites cover the basics; these harden the notification
flows).

### `ChangedFileRowInvalidationTests` flaked only inside the full serial `app-test` run — FIXED (beta.24 gate)

**Fixed:** `ChangedFileOpenTests.swift`'s two `.filePathEditor` tests restored the key in `defer` but
never drained the run loop, so the restore's `@Default` change notification (delivered async — see
`ChangesPanel.swift`'s `filePathEditorID` comment: `@EnvironmentObject`/`@State`/`@Default` invalidate
PAST the row's Equatable gate by design) could land inside the very next test class's window. In the
2258-test full serial suite that landed inside `ChangedFileRowInvalidationTests`'s tight 0.6s `settle()`
and ticked `ChangedFileRow.bodyPasses` — reproduced twice in a row during the beta.24 release gate,
clean every time in isolation. Both restores now drain the run loop first
(`restoreFilePathEditor(_:)`), closing the leak at its source rather than papering over the symptom.

### `WindowDragUITests.testDraggingWorkroomTabReordersTwoChips` is a known gesture-timing flake

**What:** Reproduced a pass then a fail on two consecutive back-to-back reruns of the identical test
against the identical binary during the beta.24 release gate — nothing else running, same machine,
same window geometry. Not caused by the beta.24 geometry fixes (fixture window 1200→1450pt): the
test computes its drag distance from the chips' own on-screen positions, so it's width-independent.

**Why:** The test's own comment already names the mechanism: "a slow drag with a hold at the end:
SwiftUI's reorder `DragGesture` needs the interpolated `onChanged` events and a settle before release
so `onEnded` commits (a fast one-shot drag can be missed)." `press(forDuration:thenDragTo:withVelocity:
thenHoldForDuration:)` synthesizes the interpolation itself, and how many intermediate events land
before the reorder's threshold check runs is not fully deterministic — occasionally too few land before
the drop, and `onEnded` sees the chip still under the threshold to swap.

**How to fix (not attempted — out of scope for the beta.24 gate, which needed to know this WASN'T a
regression, not eliminate it):** either add a manual multi-step drag (several discrete `press`+`moveTo`
calls before the final drop, giving the reorder logic more interpolated samples to react to) or lower
the reorder swap threshold's dependency on event count. Low priority: single test, single known flake
mode, not client-facing.

## P3 — Performance and diagnostics (WORKROOM-2B follow-ups)

content.description: "Split Right" menu item confirmed enabled=true via diagnostic assertion — hasTerminal FocusedValue theory was wrong. At the 1200pt fixture window width, detail column shrank to ~630pt — right on the fits() floor with no real-world margin. Fixed by widening the fixture window to 1450pt (AppStore.swift ~line 1110), leaving ~880pt for the detail column: clears the 604pt split floor with room, and stays under the ~1000pt tab-strip overflow tests need to still overflow. Diagnostic print removed from SplitPaneUITests.swift.

content.content:
1	---
2	name: curate-release
3	description: Workroom's tag-driven release process — channel architecture (stable/pre vs the side-by-side Nightly build), keeping the channel-classification logic in lockstep across Go/Swift/shell, and curating GitHub release notes after a tag publishes.
4	---
5	
6	Tag-driven (see README "Releases"). After a release publishes, **curate its GitHub release
7	notes** — replace GoReleaser's raw commit list with a succinct, themed summary in the style of
8	`v2.0.0-beta.1` (a headline, a one-line framing, and grouped bullets). The commit list is what
9	the git log is for.
10	
11	**Release channels** (issue #91) ship as **two products**. The **main** product (`workroom` CLI +
12	"Workroom" app) tracks `stable` or `pre`, chosen at runtime (`workroom update --channel stable|pre`;
13	the app's Settings picker). **Nightly** is a **separate side-by-side install** — a `workroom-nightly`
14	binary (baked `-X main.channel=nightly`) and a distinct "Workroom Nightly" app (`Nightly` build
15	config in `project.yml`: bundle id `…workroom.nightly`, `AppIcon-Nightly`, `WorkroomReleaseChannel`
16	Info.plist marker). Channel is a runtime pref for stable/pre, a build identity for nightly, so
17	nothing can drift/collide (the main binary rejects `--channel nightly`).

---
name: curate-release
description: Workroom's tag-driven release process — channel architecture (stable/pre vs the side-by-side Nightly build), keeping the channel-classification logic in lockstep across Go/Swift/shell, and curating GitHub release notes after a tag publishes.
---

Tag-driven (see README "Releases"). After a release publishes, **curate its GitHub release
notes** — replace GoReleaser's raw commit list with a succinct, themed summary in the style of
`v2.0.0-beta.1` (a headline, a one-line framing, and grouped bullets). The commit list is what
the git log is for.

**Release channels** (issue #91) ship as **two products**. The **main** product (`workroom` CLI +
"Workroom" app) tracks `stable` or `pre`, chosen at runtime (`workroom update --channel stable|pre`;
the app's Settings picker). **Nightly** is a **separate side-by-side install** — a `workroom-nightly`
binary (baked `-X main.channel=nightly`) and a distinct "Workroom Nightly" app (`Nightly` build
config in `project.yml`: bundle id `…workroom.nightly`, `AppIcon-Nightly`, `WorkroomReleaseChannel`
Info.plist marker). Channel is a runtime pref for stable/pre, a build identity for nightly, so
nothing can drift/collide (the main binary rejects `--channel nightly`).

Canonical tag→channel classification is `internal/channel` (Go), mirrored by
`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ReleaseChannel.swift` and `macapp/Scripts/channel-helper.sh` — **keep the
three in lockstep**. The updater selects per channel (stable = `/releases/latest` for byte-parity;
pre = `/releases` list, newest stable-or-prerelease; nightly = the fixed `nightly` release by tag),
orders nightlies by the monotonic commit-count and everything else by semver, and verifies against
`checksums.txt`. Nightly is a scheduled build (`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`, daily cron;
`CONFIGURATION=Nightly make app-release`) on a fixed `nightly` prerelease; all appcast-writing
workflows share a `concurrency: appcast-feed` group.

## Deployment & Releases

There is no server to deploy — Workroom is a desktop app plus a CLI distributed through **GitHub
Releases**. "Deployment" here means cutting a release: GitHub Actions builds and publishes both
components automatically when you push a version tag.

### Continuous integration

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every push to `master` and every PR against it:

- **`cli` job** (`ubuntu-latest`): sets up Go from `go.mod`, runs `golangci-lint` (subsumes `go vet`
  / `gofmt`), `go build`, and `go test ./...`.
- **`app` job** (`macos-15`): sets up Xcode + Go, `brew install xcodegen jj`, runs `make app-lint`
  (swift-format `--strict`) and `make app-test` with **ad-hoc signing** flags (hosted runners have
  no signing cert), e.g.:

  ```
  CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=
  ```

### Cutting a release

Releases are **tag-driven**. Push a `v*` tag and `.github/workflows/release.yml` does the rest:

```bash
git tag v1.4.0
git push origin v1.4.0
```

A clean `vX.Y.Z` tag publishes as a normal ("Latest") release; a tag with a prerelease component
(e.g. `v2.0.0-beta.1`, `v1.4.0-rc1`) is auto-marked as a GitHub **pre-release** so it never becomes
"Latest" (GoReleaser `prerelease: auto`).

You can test the CLI build locally with [GoReleaser](https://goreleaser.com/) before tagging
(produces binaries in `dist/` without publishing):

```bash
goreleaser build --snapshot --clean
```

**After a release publishes, curate its GitHub release notes** — replace GoReleaser's raw commit
list with a succinct, themed summary (a headline, a one-line framing, and grouped bullets). Editing
the release notes also triggers `appcast-notes.yml`, which re-renders the Sparkle update dialog's
notes from your curated body.

### Release channels

Channels are delivered as **two products**, not one switchable install:

- **Main product** — one install (the `workroom` CLI and the "Workroom" app) that tracks **stable**
  or **pre**, chosen at runtime (`workroom update --channel stable|pre`, or the app's *Settings ▸
  General ▸ Release channel*). Mutually exclusive; no side-by-side.
- **Nightly product** — a **separate download** (the `workroom-nightly` CLI and a distinct "Workroom
  Nightly" app: own bundle id `…workroom.nightly`, name, violet icon) pinned to nightly, running
  **alongside** the main install (and the Debug "Workroom Dev" build). Channel here is a *build
  identity*, not a runtime preference, so nothing can drift or collide.

| Channel | Source | Appcast tagging | Delivered as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stable` | clean `vX.Y.Z` tags | untagged (Sparkle default — everyone) | main app / `workroom` |
| `pre` | `vX.Y.Z-beta.N` / `-rc` / `-alpha` tags | `<sparkle:channel>pre</sparkle:channel>` | main app / `workroom` |
| `nightly` | daily build off `master` | `<sparkle:channel>nightly</sparkle:channel>` | Workroom Nightly / `workroom-nightly` |

build — `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` runs on a daily cron (and `workflow_dispatch`), building the

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(macapp): close cross-launch state leaks and geometry gaps in UI tests

The full local test gate for beta.24 surfaced several real bugs, not just
flakes: UI-test fixture launches share the real Dev UserDefaults domain, so
one test's sidebar toggle/drag-resize silently leaked into later launches
(fixture and non-fixture alike). Fixed by forcing sidebarVisible and pinning
sidebarWidth/inspectorWidth in UITestFixture, and gating persistsSidebarPrefs
off during fixture runs so toggles stop writing back into the real domain.

That same width squeeze (sidebar + the always-forced inspector) pushed the
fixture window's detail column under two independent floors:
TerminalSessions.fits()'s split-pane minimum and DiffViewer's
sideBySideMinWidth — silently refusing splits and collapsing side-by-side
diffs. Fixed by widening the fixture window from 1200 to 1450pt.

Also: drains the run loop after restoring .filePathEditor in
ChangedFileOpenTests so its async Defaults change notification can't leak
into ChangedFileRowInvalidationTests' tight settle window, and gives
GhosttySurfaceView a fixture-only accessibilityPlaceholderValue backdoor so
the Investigate UI test can assert on the seeded pty command directly
instead of waiting on real claude output that never renders past its
first-run trust prompt.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED
EOF
)"

content.subject: Root-caused: not a focus race, a geometry floor
content.description: "Split Right" menu item confirmed enabled=true via diagnostic assertion — hasTerminal FocusedValue theory was wrong. Real cause: TerminalSessions.fits() refuses a split when the halved pane would drop below minPaneWidth(300)*2+dividerThickness(4)=604pt. UITestFixture.applyFixtureDefaults has always forced the right inspector open (300pt); the new sidebarVisible fixture force adds the sidebar (270pt) on top. At the 1200pt fixture window width, detail column shrank to ~630pt — right on the fits() floor with no real-world margin. Fixed by widening the fixture window to 1450pt (AppStore.swift ~line 1110), leaving ~880pt for the detail column: clears the 604pt split floor with room, and stays under the ~1000pt tab-strip overflow tests need to still overflow. Diagnostic print removed from SplitPaneUITests.swift.

content.description: All 13+ discriminating tests now pass. content.subject: Root-caused: not a focus race, a geometry floor
content.description: "Split Right" menu item confirmed enabled=true via diagnostic assertion — hasTerminal FocusedValue theory was wrong. Real cause: TerminalSessions.fits() refuses a split when the halved pane would drop below minPaneWidth(300)*2+dividerThickness(4)=604pt. UITestFixture.applyFixtureDefaults has always forced the right inspector open (300pt); the new sidebarVisible fixture force adds the sidebar (270pt) on top. At the 1200pt fixture window width, detail column shrank to ~630pt — right on the fits() floor with no real-world margin. Fixed by widening the fixture window to 1450pt (AppStore.swift ~line 1110), leaving ~880pt for the detail column: clears the 604pt split floor with room, and stays under the ~1000pt tab-strip overflow tests need to still overflow. Diagnostic print removed from SplitPaneUITests.swift.

content.subject: Verify geometry fix (1450pt window) across all affected classes
content.description: All 13+ discriminating tests now pass. Root causes: (1) fits() geometry floor fixed by widening fixture window 1200→1450pt; (2) DiffViewerUITests.testSideBySideRendersTwoColumns fixed by pinning sidebarWidth/inspectorWidth in UITestFixture.applyFixtureDefaults (real domain had drifted to 406/281 from an old drag-resize test, pushing detail column under DiffViewer.sideBySideMinWidth=700); (3) WorkroomWorkflowUITests.testAppLaunchesWithChrome fixed by (a) gating persistsSidebarPrefs on !UITestFixture.isActive so future fixture toggles stop polluting the real Dev domain, and (b) one-time restore of the currently-stuck real sidebar.visible default back to true. All confirmed via xcresulttool.

content.subject: Root-caused: not a focus race, a geometry floor
content.description: "Split Right" menu item confirmed enabled=true via diagnostic assertion — hasTerminal FocusedValue theory was wrong. Real cause: TerminalSessions.fits() refuses a split when the halved pane would drop below minPaneWidth(300)*2+dividerThickness(4)=604pt. UITestFixture.applyFixtureDefaults has always forced the right inspector open (300pt); the new sidebarVisible fixture force adds the sidebar (270pt) on top. At the 1200pt fixture window width, detail column shrank to ~630pt — right on the fits() floor with no real-world margin. Fixed by widening the fixture window to 1450pt (AppStore.swift ~line 1110), leaving ~880pt for the detail column: clears the 604pt split floor with room, and stays under the ~1000pt tab-strip overflow tests need to still overflow. Diagnostic print removed from SplitPaneUITests.swift.

- Rerun: got *worse* — ~30 failures now, spread across `VCSCommitIntegrationTests`, `WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests`, `VCSProviderConformanceTests`, `VCSRemoteIntegrationTests` — every JJ/git integration test class.

Getting broader on retry, not narrower, points to a parallel-worker race: `make app-test` defaults to `-parallel-testing-enabled YES` (Makefile comment already documents this exact class of flake — shared state racing across parallel xctest workers), and both `ci.yml` and `release.yml` use that same default. These integration tests spin up real jj/git repos on disk; under parallel workers they can race on shared state. `ci.yml` happened to dodge it this run, `release.yml` didn't — twice.

Not caused by my beta.24 diff — none of it touches VCS/jj code.

2. Force serial testing for this job (`APP_TEST_FLAGS=` override in `release.yml`, matching the Makefile's own documented bisect trick) — fixes it properly but is a workflow-file change I'd want your OK on before pushing.

        # pre-tapped but untrusted on the runner image, which would otherwise emit a "tap trust"
        # warning annotation unrelated to our formulae.
        run: |
          brew untap aws/tap
          brew install xcodegen create-dmg getsentry/tools/sentry-cli protobuf

      # `make app-release` builds the Rust VCS core universal (build-apple.sh --universal). Homebrew
      # rust can't cross-compile, so ensure rustup has both darwin targets (the runner's stable is
      # current, satisfying jj-lib's 1.93 MSRV).
      - name: Add Rust darwin targets (universal VCS core)
        run: rustup target add x86_64-apple-darwin aarch64-apple-darwin

      - name: Import Developer ID signing certificate
        env:
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PWD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PWD }}
          KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          CERT="$RUNNER_TEMP/dev-id.p12"
          KEYCHAIN="$RUNNER_TEMP/app-signing.keychain-db"
          echo "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE" | openssl base64 -d -A > "$CERT"
          security create-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"
          security set-keychain-settings -lut 21600 "$KEYCHAIN"
          security unlock-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"
          security import "$CERT" -P "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PWD" -A -t cert -f pkcs12 -k "$KEYCHAIN"
          security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple: -k "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"
          security list-keychain -d user -s "$KEYCHAIN" login.keychain

      - name: Build, sign, notarize, staple, package DMG
        env:
          NOTARY_KEY: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_KEY }}
          NOTARY_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_KEY_ID }}
          NOTARY_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_ISSUER_ID }}
          # Sparkle: injects the tag as the app version and EdDSA-signs the DMG for the appcast.
          # Empty until the secret is added — release.sh then skips signing (DMG still ships).
          SPARKLE_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.SPARKLE_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          VERSION: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          # Sentry dSYM upload (optional — release.sh skips when any is empty). ORG/PROJECT are
          # slugs, not secrets, but kept as secrets here to match this job's convention.
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
        run: |
          echo "$NOTARY_KEY" | openssl base64 -d -A > "$RUNNER_TEMP/notary.p8"
          NOTARY_KEY_PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/notary.p8" make app-test APP_SIGN_FLAGS="CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=YES DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="
          NOTARY_KEY_PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/notary.p8" make app-release

      - name: Upload installer to the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          # Name matches the CLI archives' scheme; ${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v} drops the tag's leading
          # v so it lines up with goreleaser's {{ .Version }} (e.g. workroom-macos-app_1.4.0.dmg).

Attempt 3 failed too — but here's the update: attempts 2 and 3 failed the **exact same 32 tests**, byte-for-byte identical. That's not a race (a race would vary which tests fail); it's deterministic. Rules out random parallel-worker flakiness.

New lead: `release.yml`'s `app-test` step runs right after importing a **real Developer ID cert**, with `CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=YES` — a genuinely signed test binary, not ad-hoc (`ci.yml` uses plain ad-hoc, no cert imported). Every one of the 32 failures is a VCS *integration* test that shells out to real `jj`/`git` or does real subprocess/file I/O. A hardened-runtime/real-signed test binary can behave differently for subprocess spawning than an ad-hoc one — that's my leading hypothesis for why this only breaks in the release job specifically, not `ci.yml`, not locally.

Attempt 1's smaller 5-failure set vs attempts 2/3's 32 is likely just cache state (first run hit a partially-stale VCS core artifact; once that cleared, the real signing-related break showed consistently).

This isn't caused by anything in the beta.24 diff — genuine, pre-existing CI/release-workflow gap. I've used the one retry you approved; not rerunning again on my own.

Given this, your earlier options stand, refined:
2. Force serial isn't the fix now (it's not a race) — the real fix would be figuring out why real-signing breaks these tests (e.g. `CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual` picking the wrong/no identity, or hardened-runtime restricting subprocess spawn) and adjusting `release.yml`'s test-phase signing flags.
3. Build/sign/notarize/DMG locally myself and upload the asset by hand to unblock this release now, investigate the CI signing issue separately.

# build reuses these checkouts via the same -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath, so it won't re-clone.
      #
      # Skipped on an exact cache hit: there's nothing to clone, so the whole step (~25s, including an
      # xcodegen run that `make app-test` does again anyway) is pure overhead. A restore-keys-only
      # (partial) restore reports no cache-hit, so a dependency change still resolves here, retries
      # and all.
      - name: Resolve SPM packages (retry on network flake)
        if: steps.spm.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        working-directory: macapp
        run: |
          xcodegen generate
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            xcodebuild -project WorkroomApp.xcodeproj -scheme WorkroomApp \
              -derivedDataPath DerivedData -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages \
              -resolvePackageDependencies && exit 0
            echo "::warning::SPM resolve attempt $attempt failed; retrying in 15s"
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "::error::SPM resolve failed after 3 attempts"; exit 1

      # Hosted runners have no signing cert / dev team: ad-hoc sign, clear the team, manual
      # style so xcodebuild won't provision against Apple's servers. Lets the non-sandboxed
      # app build and the unit tests launch their host app. (`make app-test` also builds.)
      - name: Test
        run: >-
          make app-test
          APP_SIGN_FLAGS="CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=YES DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="

content.subject: Root-caused: not a focus race, a geometry floor
content.description: "Split Right" menu item confirmed enabled=true via diagnostic assertion — hasTerminal FocusedValue theory was wrong. Real cause: TerminalSessions.fits() refuses a split when the halved pane would drop below minPaneWidth(300)*2+dividerThickness(4)=604pt. UITestFixture.applyFixtureDefaults has always forced the right inspector open (300pt); the new sidebarVisible fixture force adds the sidebar (270pt) on top. At the 1200pt fixture window width, detail column shrank to ~630pt — right on the fits() floor with no real-world margin. Fixed by widening the fixture window to 1450pt (AppStore.swift ~line 1110), leaving ~880pt for the detail column: clears the 604pt split floor with room, and stays under the ~1000pt tab-strip overflow tests need to still overflow. Diagnostic print removed from SplitPaneUITests.swift.

content.subject: Verify geometry fix (1450pt window) across all affected classes
content.description: All 13+ discriminating tests now pass. Root causes: (1) fits() geometry floor fixed by widening fixture window 1200→1450pt; (2) DiffViewerUITests.testSideBySideRendersTwoColumns fixed by pinning sidebarWidth/inspectorWidth in UITestFixture.applyFixtureDefaults (real domain had drifted to 406/281 from an old drag-resize test, pushing detail column under DiffViewer.sideBySideMinWidth=700); (3) WorkroomWorkflowUITests.testAppLaunchesWithChrome fixed by (a) gating persistsSidebarPrefs on !UITestFixture.isActive so future fixture toggles stop polluting the real Dev domain, and (b) one-time restore of the currently-stuck real sidebar.visible default back to true. All confirmed via xcresulttool.

name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: write

# Serialize with the nightly + appcast-notes workflows: all three download-modify-upload the same
# appcast.xml, so overlapping runs could drop items. Queue rather than cancel.
concurrency:
  group: appcast-feed
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod

      - uses: goreleaser/goreleaser-action@v7
        with:
          version: "~> v2"
          args: release --clean
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

  # Build a Developer ID-signed, notarized, stapled Workroom.dmg and attach it to the release
  # goreleaser created above. Requires repo secrets: MACOS_CERTIFICATE / MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PWD
  # (base64 .p12 + password), KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD, and the App Store Connect notary API key
  # NOTARY_KEY / NOTARY_KEY_ID / NOTARY_ISSUER_ID.
  # Optional: SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN / SENTRY_ORG / SENTRY_PROJECT enable Sentry dSYM upload so release
  # crashes symbolicate; release.sh skips that step when any of them (or sentry-cli) is absent.
  macapp:
    needs: release
    runs-on: macos-15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: maxim-lobanov/setup-xcode@v1
        with:
          xcode-version: latest-stable

      # Scripts/build-helper.sh compiles + embeds the workroom CLI into the app bundle.
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod

      - name: Install XcodeGen + create-dmg + sentry-cli + protobuf
        # sentry-cli uploads dSYMs in release.sh (skipped there if the Sentry env vars are unset).
        # protobuf provides protoc, a build-time dep of the Rust VCS core (jj-lib). aws/tap ships
        # pre-tapped but untrusted on the runner image, which would otherwise emit a "tap trust"
        # warning annotation unrelated to our formulae.
        run: |
          brew untap aws/tap
          brew install xcodegen create-dmg getsentry/tools/sentry-cli protobuf

      # `make app-release` builds the Rust VCS core universal (build-apple.sh --universal). Homebrew
      # rust can't cross-compile, so ensure rustup has both darwin targets (the runner's stable is
      # current, satisfying jj-lib's 1.93 MSRV).
      - name: Add Rust darwin targets (universal VCS core)
        run: rustup target add x86_64-apple-darwin aarch64-apple-darwin

      - name: Import Developer ID signing certificate
        env:
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PWD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PWD }}
          KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          CERT="$RUNNER_TEMP/dev-id.p12"
          KEYCHAIN="$RUNNER_TEMP/app-signing.keychain-db"
          echo "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE" | openssl base64 -d -A > "$CERT"
          security create-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"
          security set-keychain-settings -lut 21600 "$KEYCHAIN"
          security unlock-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"
          security import "$CERT" -P "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PWD" -A -t cert -f pkcs12 -k "$KEYCHAIN"
          security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple: -k "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"
          security list-keychain -d user -s "$KEYCHAIN" login.keychain

      - name: Build, sign, notarize, staple, package DMG
        env:
          NOTARY_KEY: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_KEY }}
          NOTARY_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_KEY_ID }}
          NOTARY_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_ISSUER_ID }}
          # Sparkle: injects the tag as the app version and EdDSA-signs the DMG for the appcast.
          # Empty until the secret is added — release.sh then skips signing (DMG still ships).
          SPARKLE_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.SPARKLE_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          VERSION: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          # Sentry dSYM upload (optional — release.sh skips when any is empty). ORG/PROJECT are
          # slugs, not secrets, but kept as secrets here to match this job's convention.
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
        run: |
          echo "$NOTARY_KEY" | openssl base64 -d -A > "$RUNNER_TEMP/notary.p8"
          NOTARY_KEY_PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/notary.p8" make app-test APP_SIGN_FLAGS="CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=YES DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="
          NOTARY_KEY_PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/notary.p8" make app-release

      - name: Upload installer to the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          # Name matches the CLI archives' scheme; ${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v} drops the tag's leading
          # v so it lines up with goreleaser's {{ .Version }} (e.g. workroom-macos-app_1.4.0.dmg).
          ASSET="$RUNNER_TEMP/workroom-macos-app_${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}.dmg"
          cp macapp/build/release/Workroom.dmg "$ASSET"
          gh release upload "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" "$ASSET" --clobber

      - name: Publish Sparkle appcast
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: macapp/Scripts/appcast.sh

content.description: "Split Right" menu item confirmed enabled=true via diagnostic assertion — hasTerminal FocusedValue theory was wrong. Real cause: TerminalSessions.fits() refuses a split when the halved pane would drop below minPaneWidth(300)*2+dividerThickness(4)=604pt. content.content:
## workroom 2.0 — now with a native macOS app

The headline of 2.0 is a **native macOS app** (macOS 14+): a SwiftUI interface with a
project → workroom sidebar and embedded terminals. The CLI ships bundled, so app users
don't need a separate install — and it stays fully standalone for terminal-first use on
macOS, Linux, and Windows.

> ⚠️ This is a beta — expect rough edges.

### macOS app
- Project → workroom tree sidebar, with an always-available project root
- Embedded terminals: multiple tabs per workroom, drag-to-reorder, copy-on-select,
  ⌘-click to open file paths, and activity notifications
- "Open in…" menu that remembers your last editor; offer to open new workrooms in `$EDITOR`
- Streamed setup/teardown script output in a log panel
- Settings window, light/dark/system theme, and Sparkle auto-updates
- "Install workroom Command in PATH" helper, plus a new app icon

### CLI
- New setup/teardown script env vars: `WORKROOM_PATH` and `WORKROOM_ROOT_PATH`
- Machine-readable `--json` API that powers the app

### Build & CI
- GitHub Actions CI; runs macOS app tests/lint and ships a notarized DMG
- `golangci-lint` and `swift-format` wired in
- Unified, namespaced root `Makefile`

## Diffs that agree with your VCS

This beta is mostly about **trusting what you see**: the git diff layer now matches `git` itself
(renames included), jj reports per-file conflicts and rename/copy detection, and History rows say
what's pushed and where the refs are. Tab strips, splits, and the Markdown preview all got a
polish pass, and terminals finally inherit your real login-shell environment.

> ⚠️ Still a beta — expect rough edges.

### Diffs & VCS core
- The git diff layer now **agrees with `git` itself** — rename detection in commit diffs, and a
  merge working copy diffed against its first parent
- jj: **per-file conflict status**, rename/copy detection, log and branch labels ordered
  topologically (not by committer time), and changed lines counted in the native read
- Working-copy status survives a single unreadable blob instead of failing the whole read; jj
  snapshots are serialized across the status fan-out; the jj error taxonomy (lock contention,
  staleness) is actually reachable now
- Git working line counts read through libgit2 directly — faster status refreshes

### Changes & History
- Branch/bookmark and ref chips in the **Changes** header (pilled, left of the author), with the
  card's duplicate dropped
- History rows show an **unpushed** status and are decorated with branch/tag refs
- History sidebar rows keep avatars and drop author names; the Changes file list matches History's
  path styling
- Conflicted-file badge and its sidebar aggregate are now UI-tested

### Tabs, splits & panes
- A selected tab **scrolls into view** in both tab strips — including a chip that only appears
  after its selection, and one revealed when a strip first appears
- Workroom tab chips cap their title and take the selected-terminal-tab styling
- New **Remove from Split** context-menu action (#122)
- Panes get a real minimum *width* (separate from height), the pane floor applies to two split
  paths that skipped it, and a narrow window no longer erases the stored split ratio
- The tab strips' "+" stays reachable and off the toolbar (#129)

### Keyboard, menus & chrome
- **⌘B / ⌥⌘B** toggle the Inspector and the Projects sidebar
- View-menu shortcuts are reserved under a focused TUI, and ⌥⌘S no longer pops the native sidebar
- Activity-bar tooltips name their action, and the bell shows its key hint
- The open file's path now shows in the pane footer (#136)
- Inspector section layout is global, not per-workroom

### Markdown preview
- **Mermaid loads on demand** instead of on every Markdown open
- A loader shows while the preview boots
- Raw HTML tags no longer truncate the preview; non-rendering container tags are escaped

### Fixes
- Terminals resolve their child environment from your **login shell**, so your real PATH and tools
  are there
- New/Open Workroom dialogs are actually blocking
- Project delete clears pending sheets, including across windows (#127)
- Run opens its settings sheet with a warning when no command is configured
- CLI: `add-project --pretend` is honored without `--create`

### Build & CI
- The build fails when the linked Rust VCS core is stale (and the universal build no longer fails
  its own staleness gate)
- Unit tests run in parallel; CI caches the Xcode build dir and skips the Rust core build and

content.subject: Root-caused: not a focus race, a geometry floor
content.description: "Split Right" menu item confirmed enabled=true via diagnostic assertion — hasTerminal FocusedValue theory was wrong. Real cause: TerminalSessions.fits() refuses a split when the halved pane would drop below minPaneWidth(300)*2+dividerThickness(4)=604pt. UITestFixture.applyFixtureDefaults has always forced the right inspector open (300pt); the new sidebarVisible fixture force adds the sidebar (270pt) on top. At the 1200pt fixture window width, detail column shrank to ~630pt — right on the fits() floor with no real-world margin. Fixed by widening the fixture window to 1450pt (AppStore.swift ~line 1110), leaving ~880pt for the detail column: clears the 604pt split floor with room, and stays under the ~1000pt tab-strip overflow tests need to still overflow. Diagnostic print removed from SplitPaneUITests.swift.

content.subject: Verify geometry fix (1450pt window) across all affected classes
content.description: All 13+ discriminating tests now pass. Root causes: (1) fits() geometry floor fixed by widening fixture window 1200→1450pt; (2) DiffViewerUITests.testSideBySideRendersTwoColumns fixed by pinning sidebarWidth/inspectorWidth in UITestFixture.applyFixtureDefaults (real domain had drifted to 406/281 from an old drag-resize test, pushing detail column under DiffViewer.sideBySideMinWidth=700); (3) WorkroomWorkflowUITests.testAppLaunchesWithChrome fixed by (a) gating persistsSidebarPrefs on !UITestFixture.isActive so future fixture toggles stop polluting the real Dev domain, and (b) one-time restore of the currently-stuck real sidebar.visible default back to true. input.content:
## A quick switcher, a real VCS toolbar, and sessions that survive a restart

The big one this beta: **⌥Tab / ⌃Tab quick switching** between workrooms and panes, a **VCS
toolbar** with commit-from-Changes, and full **session restore** — windows, panels, splits, and
even scrollback come back after you quit and relaunch. 58 theme families now, up from 27.

> ⚠️ Still a beta — expect rough edges.

### Quick switcher (issue #132)
- **⌥Tab** cycles open workrooms by recency across every window; **⌃Tab** cycles the current
  workroom's panes
- A label-led rail with per-switcher card identities, Liquid Glass styling, and a proper drop
  shadow that doesn't kill the glass
- Go-menu items for both switchers, so they're mouse-reachable and self-documenting
- Contrast metric fixed to be actually WCAG (rail floors + VoiceOver watch) — this bug affected
  every theme, not just the switcher

### VCS toolbar & commit
- A **VCS toolbar** across the top of the inspector, with room for its content above and below
- **Commit from the Changes inspector**, with a second, named verb instead of hiding it
- Sync-count pills moved onto the title line; VCS failures surface in a dialog instead of a
  truncated toolbar line
- jj ahead/behind now counts against trunk, and jj **Pull rebases**; remotes read from config,
  not remote-tracking refs
- jj reads your **real jj config** (`~/.config/jj/config.toml`), not jj-lib's empty built-in
  defaults — commits and signing now carry your actual identity

### Sessions & windows that survive a restart (#46, #144, #145)
- Every open window, panel, and layout is **restored across restarts** — including terminal
  **scrollback** in restored panes
- Offer to **resume an agent session** in a restored pane instead of starting cold
- The Projects sidebar's open/closed state persists across relaunch too

### Panes, tabs & chrome
- Every workroom gets its **own title bar and toolbar**; a window can hold several split groups
  at once, each with its own chip bracket
- **cwd actions in the pane status bar** (#143) — copy path, reveal in Finder, open a terminal
  there
- The focused workroom pane is framed and highlighted, including inside a split
- The theme picker moved to a toolbar dropdown instead of a sheet

### Fixes
- Investigate now tracks its own session instead of diverging from the run tab (#146)
- CRLF handled correctly on scrollback replay; the viewport is skipped while a TUI is up (#144)
- A cancelled `gh` probe no longer reports a failing PR as green, and stopped pinning "jj isn't
  installed" from a launch-time PATH miss
- The commit-dialog, VCS-toolbar, and quick-switcher review passes each closed out their
  remaining findings (wrong-destination commits, key routing, MRU ordering, and more)
- Diff rendering now uses `List` to fix an AttributeGraph app hang; the History pane's own
  invalidation storm is fixed too

### Build & CI
- The release workflow now installs `jj` — the VCS integration test suite needs it, and its
  absence there (unlike the regular CI job, which already had it) was silently failing every
  jj/git-colocated integration test on release cuts
- The embedded CLI now builds and asserts as universal; `release.sh` always runs `xcodegen` first
- Local dev builds never start Sentry
